brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.requirement: The build is a two-storey tower (uses two storeys).
requirements.evidence: Ground-level bases (piece 0,0,0; 1,0,0; -1,0,0 half; 0,-1,0 half) plus a base at 0,0,1 on the upper storey, joined by cover:0,0,1 and snap:0,0,0. Levels 0 and 1 are used.

requirements.requirement: The tower holds at least two drawers.
requirements.evidence: Two drawer-family parts: drawer:0#-1,0#cut (on the cut face of half-n base at -1,0,0) and drawer:0#0,-1#cut (on half-s base at 0,-1,0). Two additional notch drawer frames (notch:0#0,1 and notch:0#1,-1) are also fitted, for four drawer-type units in total. The drawer family count is 2.

requirements.requirement: The tower stays modest in size (under about 40 parts).
requirements.evidence: 14 parts in the build (get_build total 14). check_build: meshClash clear, no error or loose-body warnings; only an info note about open cap faces.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey storage tower with two drawers. Ground storey: a full base with covers and joint bolts linking two half bases, which carry the two drawers on their cut faces; two notch drawer frames sit beside the base. Upper storey: one full base on top of the centre. The build is 14 parts, mesh-clear, with no errors. The tower is a small two-level block, not a large one; the upper storey has only one cell. Covers and caps are left open on several faces (info only). The brief doesn't specify a workbench mount, so none is included; the configurator doesn't verify fit to a bench or any material properties.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
